105.s: Regarding the proposal to secure UNESCO World Heritage status for Lepakshi and Gandikota, identify the incorrect statement.
o: Gandikota is noted for temple architecture, murals and sculpture.
Gandikota is not yet on UNESCO's Tentative List.
Lepakshi is noted for temple architecture, murals and sculpture.
Lepakshi is already on UNESCO's Tentative List.
105.x: The incorrect statement is that Gandikota is noted for temple architecture, murals and sculpture. Those features are associated with Lepakshi, whereas Gandikota is known for its fort and gorge landscape.
105.tq: Negative / Incorrect Statement · tests the “UNESCO Tentative List and features” angle
n: ⚠ Lepakshi is already on the UNESCO Tentative List; Gandikota is not yet [August 2026 · Lepakshi and Gandikota: UNESCO World Heritage push]
Lepakshi: temple architecture, murals, sculpture; Gandikota: fort and gorge landscape [August 2026 · Lepakshi and Gandikota: UNESCO World Heritage push]
xs: The incorrect statement is that **Gandikota is noted for temple architecture, murals and sculpture** — option **(1)**.
Those features belong to **Lepakshi**; **Gandikota** is known for its **fort** and **gorge** landscape.
⚠ **Lepakshi** is already on the **UNESCO Tentative List**; Gandikota is not yet — so options (2), (3), (4) are true.
xa: The **Centre was urged** at a meeting with the Union Tourism and Culture Minister in New Delhi to back both sites.
**Amaravati Buddhist sculptures** preserved in **London museums** were also highlighted.
**India's World Heritage Sites (July 2026)**: **45** — **37** cultural, **7** natural, **1** mixed.
Evaluators: cultural — **ICOMOS**; natural — **IUCN**.

105.x: The eight species are four African and four Asian, so statement 3 is wrong.
n: 8 species: African — Black-bellied, White-bellied, Giant Ground, Temminck's Ground; Asian — Indian, Chinese, Sunda, Philippine [August 2026 · Rare pangolin rescued in Kamalapuram (Kadapa)]
xa: **Indian Pangolin** — IUCN **Endangered**; **Chinese Pangolin** — **Critically Endangered**.

105.s:

n: Species: Both in India; Status: Schedule I, Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 [August 2026 · Rare pangolin rescued in Kamalapuram (Kadapa)]
Species: All 8 species; Status: CITES Appendix I [August 2026 · Rare pangolin rescued in Kamalapuram (Kadapa)]
xa: **Indian Pangolin** — **Endangered**; **Chinese Pangolin** — **Critically Endangered** (IUCN).

105.s:
Consider the following statements about inscriptions in Andhra Pradesh:

2. The Gajapati-era Odia inscription in Srikakulam district was found under a Tulasi Choura at Bobbili fort.
3. Bukka Raya I led the ASI epigraphy team that discovered the Vijayanagara-era inscriptions at Sadasivakona in the Seshachalam forest.

105.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Pune copper plates of Eastern Chalukya king Vishnuvardhana II (669 CE) give the earliest reference.
Statement 2: Incorrect: it was found at the Tekkali royal palace, not Bobbili fort.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the team was led by K. Muniratnam Reddy, Director of Epigraphy at ASI, Mysuru; Bukka Raya I was a Vijayanagara ruler.

105.s:
Arrange the forms of Guntur's name in the order of their evolution:
1. Gunturu
2. Kunturu
3. Gomturu
105.x: The name evolved Kunturu → Gomturu → Gunturu; the 10th-century Ederu copper plates use Gomturu.
n: Name forms: Kunturu → Gomturu → Gunturu [August 2026 · Seventh-century inscription shows Guntur's antiquity]
10th-century Ederu copper plates: name "Gomturu" (in use 10th–14th century) [August 2026 · Seventh-century inscription shows Guntur's antiquity]
xa: The earliest reference is the **Pune copper plates** of **Vishnuvardhana II** (**Eastern Chalukya**), **669 CE**.
Highlighted by **Dr. K. Munirathnam Reddy**, ASI Director of Epigraphy.

105.s:
Consider the following about the Gajapati-era Odia inscription at Tekkali:

2. Kapilendra Deva’s kingdom extended from the Kaveri in the north to the Ganga in the south.
3. Tekkali was a former Odia zamindari of Ganjam.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
105.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; Kapilendra Deva’s kingdom ran from the Ganga in the north to the Kaveri in the south.
n: Date: likely 15th century (palaeography) — exact year not known; estampage taken [August 2026 · Gajapati-era Odia inscription at Tekkali (Srikakulam)]
Kapilendra Deva's kingdom: from Ganga (north) to Kaveri (south) [August 2026 · Gajapati-era Odia inscription at Tekkali (Srikakulam)]
Tekkali: former Odia zamindari of Ganjam [August 2026 · Gajapati-era Odia inscription at Tekkali (Srikakulam)]
xa: Found under a **Tulasi Choura** at the **Tekkali royal palace**, **Srikakulam district**.
Names "**Pratapa Kapileswara**" = Gajapati **Kapilendra Deva**; script **Odia**.
Earlier noted in the **Annual Report on Indian Epigraphy 1926–27**.

**Vijayanagara Empire** est. **1336** by **Harihara I and Bukka Raya I**.

105.s:
Consider the following about the inscriptions found at Sadasivakona:

ASI: est. 1861; DG Yadubir Singh Rawat; Vijayanagara Empire est. 1336 by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I [June 2026 · Vijayanagara-era inscriptions found in Seshachalam forest]
xa: Dated **1554**, **16th century**; languages **Telugu, Tamil, Kannada**.
**Vijayanagara Empire** est. **1336** by **Harihara I and Bukka Raya I**.
ASI DG: **Yadubir Singh Rawat**.

26.s: Which one of the following statements regarding police custody and related safeguards under the BNSS is incorrect?
o: An accused may meet an advocate during interrogation, but not throughout the interrogation.
A magistrate cannot impose a blanket condition prohibiting any further extension of police custody.
Police custody may extend to 30 days in total if it is sought in parts during the initial 40 or 60 days.
No person may be detained beyond 24 hours without being produced before a magistrate.
26.x: The incorrect statement is that police custody may extend to 30 days. Section 187(2) caps total police custody at 15 days, even when it is sought in parts. The other statements reflect the rules on access to an advocate, magistrate-imposed conditions and detention beyond 24 hours.
26.tq: Negative / Incorrect Statement · tests the “Rights during interrogation” angle
n: Magistrate cannot impose a blanket "no extension" condition; SC allowed 7 more days (within 15) [August 2026 · Police custody under BNSS Section 187(2): SC ruling]
Section 38 BNSS: accused may meet an advocate during interrogation, not throughout [August 2026 · Police custody under BNSS Section 187(2): SC ruling]
Provision: Sec 58 BNSS; Rule: No detention beyond 24 hours without magistrate [August 2026 · Police custody under BNSS Section 187(2): SC ruling]
Provision: Sec 187(2) BNSS; Rule: Police custody 15 days total, in parts, within first 40/60 days [August 2026 · Police custody under BNSS Section 187(2): SC ruling]
xs: The incorrect statement is that police custody may extend to **30 days** — option **(3)**; **Sec 187(2)** caps it at **15 days**, even in parts.
Option (1) is correct: under **Section 38 BNSS** the accused may meet an advocate **during**, not **throughout**, interrogation.
Options (2) and (4) are correct: no blanket "**no extension**" condition; **Sec 58** bars detention beyond **24 hours** without a magistrate.
xa: Custody can be sought in parts within the **initial 40/60 days**.
**Sec 187(3)**: detention up to **90 days** (death/life/10+ years) or **60 days** (others); then **default bail**.
Case: **State of Andhra Pradesh vs Suda Suresh Veera Venkata Naga Raju**.

n: Passport ≠ proof of citizenship: MEA clarification (no new policy on 24 June 2026) — passport is a travel document and may be issued to some non-citizens; Passports Act, 1967 vs Citizenship Act, 1955 [June 2026 · Polity and judiciary one-liners — June 2026]

26.s: Which one of the following Carnatic music ragas is similar to Raga Bilawal in Hindustani music?
26.x: Option (d) is correct: The Indian national anthem, Jana Gana Mana, is composed in the Carnatic raga Dheera Shankarabharanam, which corresponds to the Hindustani classical raga Bilawal. The name Shankarabharanam translates to "the ornament of Shiva," and the raga is widely regarded in music therapy for its calming and healing qualities. Option (a) is incorrect: Naṭabhairavi is a raga in Carnatic music. It corresponds to the Asavari thaat of Hindustani music. Option (b) is incorrect: Kamavardhini (popularly known as Pantuvarali) is a raga in Carnatic music; its Hindustani equivalent is Puriya Dhanashri. Option (c) is incorrect: Hanumatodi, more popularly known as Todi, is a raga in Carnatic music. The equivalent of Carnatic Todi in Hindustani is Bhairavi thaat. • Note: Dheera Shankarabharanam is associated with India's National Anthem "Jana Gana Mana". Thus, UPSC expects aspirants to develop an interconnected understanding of topics that appear in newspapers, government initiatives, cultural institutions, and national symbols, rather than trying to memorise every raga or art form separately. Questions of this nature are often designed by UPSC to maintain unpredictability and keep the cutoff balanced. It is neither practical nor necessary for an aspirant to know every such highly specific fact. We recommend aspirants avoid unnecessary guesswork in such highly factual questions.

53.s: Which statement correctly describes helium’s behaviour at very low temperatures?

53.tq: Direct Recall · tests the “Boiling point and solidification” angle
n: Boiling point: about -269°C (−268.9°C) — lowest of all; cannot solidify at normal pressure (needs ~25 atm at ~1 K) [July 2026 · China's helium export ban]
xs: Helium boils at about **-269°C** and **cannot solidify at normal pressure** — option **(4)**.
It needs **~25 atm** at ~1 K to solidify, so option (2) is wrong; **25°C** and **1°C** are not its boiling point.
xa: Helium has the **lowest** boiling point of all elements (−268.9°C).
It is moved in **vacuum-jacketed stainless steel** vessels; **boil-off** is a risk.
Commercial purity is **99.997%**.

n: NITI Aayog: est. 1 January 2015 (replaced Planning Commission); chair PM; Vice-Chairperson Ashok Kumar Lahiri; CEO Anurag Jain [August 2026 · NITI Aayog: four sectors for a global manufacturing hub]
xs: Both are true, but R is **not the correct explanation** of A — option **(2)**.
A is true: **NITI Aayog** was set up on **1 January 2015**, replacing the **Planning Commission**.
R is true: the **PM** chairs it, but that does not explain its founding date.
xa: Vice-Chairperson: **Ashok Kumar Lahiri**.
CEO: **Anurag Jain**.

19.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

19.s:

Statement 3: Correct: Operation Sindoor marked the first time India and Pakistan integrated cyber operations into an active conflict.

PRAHAAR Framework: intelligence-led, pre-emptive deterrence; decouples terrorism from religion [July 2026 · Global Terrorism Index 2026]

19.s: Which of the following statements about the findings of the Global Terrorism Index 2026 is incorrect?
o: About 93% of terrorism-related deaths occurred in conflict-affected or unstable countries.
Terrorism incidents in 2025 fell by 22% to about 2,944.
A total of 81 countries improved in the index findings for 2025.
Terrorism-related deaths in 2025 fell by 28% to about 5,582.

19.tq: Negative / Incorrect Statement · tests the “Global terrorism trends” angle
n: 2025: deaths down 28% (about 5,582); incidents down 22% (about 2,944); 81 countries improved [July 2026 · Global Terrorism Index 2026]
99% of deaths in conflict-affected / unstable countries [July 2026 · Global Terrorism Index 2026]
xs: The incorrect statement is that **93%** of deaths occurred in conflict-affected/unstable countries — the figure is **99%** — option **(1)** is the answer.
Incidents fell **22%** to about **2,944** — correct.
**81 countries** improved — correct.
Deaths fell **28%** to about **5,582** — correct.
xa: ⚠ **93%** is a different figure: the share of fatal attacks in the **West** (last 5 years) by **lone actors**.
**60%+** of attacks occurred within **100 km** of borders.
Major groups: **Islamic State**, **JNIM**, **TTP**, **Lashkar-e-Taiba**, **Al-Shabaab**.

19.s: With reference to UNICEF's Children's Climate Risk Report 2026, identify the incorrect statement.
o: 392 million children in India, or 92%, were exposed to extreme heat.
India's air-pollution score was 8.84 out of 10.
India's drought score was 8.84 out of 10.
89 million children in India faced recurring heatwaves.
19.x: The incorrect statement is that India's air-pollution score was 8.84; the correct score was 9.94 out of 10. The score of 8.84 applied to the drought indicator, while the child-exposure figures are 392 million and 89 million.
19.tq: Negative / Incorrect Statement · tests the “Children exposed to climate hazards” angle
n: India: 392 million (92%) children exposed to extreme heat; 89 million face recurring heatwaves [June 2026 · UNICEF Children's Climate Risk Report 2026]
Indicator: Air pollution; India's score: 9.94/10 [June 2026 · UNICEF Children's Climate Risk Report 2026]
Indicator: Drought; India's score: 8.84/10 [June 2026 · UNICEF Children's Climate Risk Report 2026]
xs: The incorrect statement is that India's **air-pollution** score was **8.84** — it was **9.94/10** — option **(2)** is the answer.
**8.84/10** is India's **drought** score — correct.
**392 million (92%)** children exposed to **extreme heat** and **89 million** facing recurring heatwaves — correct.
xa: India's overall climate risk: **9.21/10**; extreme heat **10/10**.
⚠ In South Asia only **Pakistan (9.44)** and **Bangladesh (9.38)** scored higher.
World: ~**1.1 billion** children face **3+** hazards at once.

1. Global forced displacement increased from 117.8 million to 123.2 million.
2. At the end of 2025 there were 41.6 million refugees and 68.6 million internally displaced persons.
3. 14.7 million people returned home, including 4.4 million refugees and 10.3 million IDPs.
Which of the above statements are correct?
19.x: 2 and 3 are correct; displacement actually fell from 123.2 million to 117.8 million, the first decline in a decade.
n: Forced displacement: 123.2 → 117.8 million in 2025 — ⚠ first decline in a decade [June 2026 · UNHCR Global Trends — first decline in displacement]
End-2025: 41.6 million refugees, 68.6 million IDPs [June 2026 · UNHCR Global Trends — first decline in displacement]

Returned home (2025): 14.7 million (4.4 mn refugees + 10.3 mn IDPs) — most to Afghanistan, Sudan, Syria; 32.3 million new internal displacements [June 2026 · UNHCR Global Trends — first decline in displacement]
xa: Most returns were to **Afghanistan, Sudan, Syria**.
**32.3 million** new internal displacements.
**UNHCR**: est. **1950**, **Geneva**.

19.s: According to the State of India's Digital Economy 2026 report, which statement correctly describes India's position in the global AI ecosystem?

About 19.9% of global AI users are Indian, and India is the fourth-largest AI talent hub
About 19.9% of global AI users are Indian, and India is the second-largest AI talent hub

n: AI users: ~19.9% of global AI users are Indian; India 2nd-largest AI talent hub [June 2026 · State of India's Digital Economy (SIDE) 2026]

CHIPS: **Connect, Harness, Innovate, Protect, Sustain**.
**ICRIER** est. **1981**, New Delhi.

19.s:
Consider the following statements about child mortality, cyber-fraud and fiscal deficits:

2. By 2050, one in five Indians is projected to be aged 60 or above.

19.s:

Iceland is followed by New Zealand, Ireland, Denmark and Austria. Seven of the ten countries at the top of the GPI are in Europe. India ranked 115th out of 163 countries in the Global Peace Index 2025.

87.s:

87.s:

Penalty: Daily default fine; Old: ₹100/day; New: ₹1,000/day [March 2026 · AP Legislative Assembly passes three Bills (March 4, 2026)]

**NOC replaced by Fire Safety Certificate**, **"Emergency Service"** status, and fine **₹500 → ₹10,000** are correct.

87.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Governor's options under Article 200 is incorrect?
o: The Governor may assent to a Bill.
The Governor may withhold assent to a Bill.
The Governor may return a Bill if it is not a Money Bill.
The Governor may return a Money Bill to the House for reconsideration.
87.x: The incorrect statement is that the Governor may return a Money Bill: under Article 200 only a Bill that is not a Money Bill can be returned. Assent, withholding assent and reserving a Bill for the President are the other options.
87.tq: Negative / Incorrect Statement · tests the “Governor's powers under Article 200” angle
n: Governor's assent: under Article 200 — assent, withhold, return (if not a Money Bill), or reserve for President [March 2026 · AP Legislative Assembly passes three Bills (March 4, 2026)]
xs: The incorrect statement is option **(4)**: a **Money Bill** cannot be **returned** for reconsideration.
Under **Article 200** the Governor may **assent**, **withhold assent**, **return** a Bill (**if not a Money Bill**) or **reserve** it for the **President** — options (1)–(3) are correct.
xa: Reservation applies to **any** Bill, a Money Bill included; only **return** is barred for Money Bills.
The provision arose for the **Public Services (Second Amendment) Bill, 2025**.
**Article 201** covers what the President does with a reserved Bill.

106.s: Which one of the following statements about land registration and records is incorrect?

Mutation by itself confers title to land.

27.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Forest Rights Act-related High Court rulings is incorrect?
o: The Allahabad High Court upheld the District Level Committee’s rejection of Tharu tribe claims.
The Madras High Court upheld eviction notices and grazing bans under the Tamil Nadu Forest Act, 1882 despite pending FRA claims.
The doctrine lex posterior derogat priori means that a later law overrides an earlier law.
Grazing rights are recognised even in national parks and sanctuaries.
27.x: The incorrect statement is the second one. The Allahabad High Court set aside, rather than upheld, the District Level Committee’s rejection of Tharu tribe claims; the other statements correctly describe the rulings and the Forest Rights Act position.
27.tq: Negative / Incorrect Statement · tests the “Contrasting High Court rulings under FRA” angle
n: Court: Allahabad HC; Ruling: Set aside DLC rejection of Tharu tribe claims (UP); FRA overrides earlier laws [May 2026 · Forest Rights Act — Allahabad vs Madras HC rulings]
Court: Madras HC; Ruling: Upheld eviction notices and grazing bans under Tamil Nadu Forest Act, 1882 despite pending FRA claims [May 2026 · Forest Rights Act — Allahabad vs Madras HC rulings]
Doctrine: lex posterior derogat priori — later law overrides earlier law [May 2026 · Forest Rights Act — Allahabad vs Madras HC rulings]
⚠ Grazing rights recognised even in national parks and sanctuaries [May 2026 · Forest Rights Act — Allahabad vs Madras HC rulings]
xs: The incorrect statement: the **Allahabad HC upheld** the DLC rejection — option **(1)**; it actually **set aside** the rejection of **Tharu** claims.
Option (2) is correct: **Madras HC** upheld eviction and grazing bans under the **Tamil Nadu Forest Act, 1882**.
Options (3) and (4) are correct: **lex posterior derogat priori** — later law overrides earlier; ⚠ grazing rights apply even in **national parks** and **sanctuaries**.
xa: Allahabad HC held the **FRA overrides** earlier laws.
Official name: **Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006**.
**Gram Sabha** central; no eviction until verification complete.

27.s:

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
27.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Clause 3 limits SC status to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists; conversion to other religions results in loss of the status.

Statement 3: Incorrect: a nine-judge Constitution Bench led by CJI Surya Kant, not a five-judge bench, is hearing the question.

27.s:

Reason (R): Active euthanasia remains legal in India.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
27.x: Assertion A is true because the Harish Rana matter marked the first actual implementation of passive euthanasia in a specific case. Reason R is false because active euthanasia remains illegal; passive euthanasia involves withholding or withdrawing life-sustaining treatment under strict conditions.
27.tq: Assertion-Reason · tests the “Passive euthanasia and active euthanasia” angle
n: Passive euthanasia: withholding/withdrawing life-sustaining treatment — legal under strict conditions [March 2026 · Right to die with dignity — Harish Rana case]
⚠ First time the SC actually implemented passive euthanasia in a specific case; active euthanasia remains illegal [March 2026 · Right to die with dignity — Harish Rana case]
xs: **A is true, but R is false** — option **(3)**.
A is true: ⚠ **first time** the SC actually implemented **passive euthanasia** in a specific case.
R is false: **active euthanasia** remains **illegal**.
xa: **Aruna Shanbaug (2011)**: passive euthanasia in exceptional cases.
**Common Cause (2018)**: **living wills**; simplified in **2023**.

27.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Assam Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026, is incorrect?

⚠ **Third** State after **Uttarakhand** and **Gujarat**; first in Northeast.

27.s: With reference to the key provisions of the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026, which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Imprisonment for minor offences may be replaced by monetary or civil penalties.
Warnings and improvement notices may precede penalties for initial contraventions.
Fines are increased by 10% every five years through periodic revision.
Enforcement is shifted from criminal courts to administrative adjudication by designated officers and appellate authorities.
27.x: The incorrect statement is that fines are increased by 10% every five years; the prescribed periodic revision is a 10% increase every three years. The other statements correctly describe civil penalties, graded compliance and administrative adjudication.
27.tq: Negative / Incorrect Statement · tests the “Enforcement mechanism” angle
n: Imprisonment replaced by monetary/civil penalties for minor offences; obsolete provisions removed [April 2026 · Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill 2026 passed]
Graded compliance: warnings and improvement notices for initial contraventions before penalties [April 2026 · Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill 2026 passed]
Enforcement shifted from criminal courts to administrative adjudication — designated officers + appellate authorities [April 2026 · Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill 2026 passed]
Periodic revision of fines — 10% increase every three years [April 2026 · Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill 2026 passed]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**10% every five years**" — option **(3)**; fines rise **10% every three years**.
Options (1), (2) and (4) are correct: imprisonment replaced by **monetary/civil penalties**; **warnings** and **improvement notices** first; **administrative adjudication**.
xa: Called **Jan Vishwas 2.0**; linked to **World Bank B-READY**.
Serious offences (public safety, environment, fraud) keep **criminal liability**.
Concern: **regulatory capture**, fines as cost of business.

Statement 1: Correct: Andhra Pradesh announced India's first human-carrier drone ambulance.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the drone ambulance is designed for beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) operations, not only EVLOS.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the AP FIRST research centre is located at Tirupati, not Vijayawada.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about AP's drone ambulance and research:
1. Dr. Nori Dattatreya provided guidance for Andhra Pradesh's human-carrier drone ambulance initiative.
2. Andhra Pradesh's human-carrier drone ambulance is being supported by the Kalam Advanced UAV Research Centre (Anna University) and IIT Hyderabad.
3. The principal research areas of the AP FIRST centre at Tirupati are aerospace, defence, space, AI, cybersecurity, semiconductors, quantum, biotechnology and green energy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: guidance was provided by G. Satheesh Reddy, former DRDO Chairman and AP's Aero Defence Adviser, not Dr. Nori Dattatreya.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the drone ambulance is supported by the Kalam Advanced UAV Research Centre at Anna University and IIT Tirupati, not IIT Hyderabad.
Statement 3: Correct: AP FIRST focuses on aerospace, defence, space, AI, cybersecurity, semiconductors, quantum, biotechnology and green energy.

101.s: With reference to AP’s human-carrier drone ambulance, which pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Proposed drone port and hub – Visakhapatnam
101.x: The proposed drone port and hub is at Vijayawada, not Visakhapatnam; the other pairs are correct.
n: Feature: Altitude; Detail: ~1,200 feet [January 2026 · India's first human-carrier drone ambulance]

Feature: Speed; Detail: 50–60 kmph [January 2026 · India's first human-carrier drone ambulance]

xa: ⚠ It operates **beyond** visual line of sight (**BVLOS**).
A **paramedic** can accompany the patient.
Guided by **G. Satheesh Reddy**.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about AP's aerospace and space-tech firsts:
1. N. Lokesh announced the establishment of India's first integrated Aviation, Aerospace and Defence (AAD) EduCity near Bhogapuram International Airport.
2. India's first integrated Aviation, Aerospace and Defence EduCity is planned near Gannavaram Airport.
3. Taramandal, a Visakhapatnam-based space-tech start-up, is developing a prototype of India's first orbital satellite data centre (60-kg class).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x:
Statement 1: Correct: HRD and IT Minister N. Lokesh announced the EduCity near Bhogapuram International Airport.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the EduCity is planned near Bhogapuram International Airport, not Gannavaram Airport.
Statement 3: Correct: Taramandal is developing India's first orbital satellite data centre prototype in the 60-kg class.

101.s: With reference to the Aviation, Aerospace and Defence (AAD) EduCity near Bhogapuram, which pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Land provided – 136 acres free of cost from MANSAS Trust
Primary aim – Bridge the human capital gap in aviation
101.x: Global university roadshows were to begin from February 2026, not 2027; the other pairs are correct.
n: Land: 136 acres free of cost from MANSAS Trust [December 2025 · India's first Aviation, Aerospace and Defence (AAD) EduCity near Bhogapuram]
Timeline: core infrastructure in 12 months; roadshows from February 2026 for global universities [December 2025 · India's first Aviation, Aerospace and Defence (AAD) EduCity near Bhogapuram]
Aim: bridge human capital gap in aviation (pilots, engineers, MRO specialists) [December 2025 · India's first Aviation, Aerospace and Defence (AAD) EduCity near Bhogapuram]
xa: Developer: **GMR Group**; announced by Minister **N. Lokesh**.
Location: near **Bhogapuram International Airport**.
AP offers land at **99 paise** to **Fortune 500** investors.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about Visakhapatnam initiatives:
1. Taramandal's orbital satellite data centre initiative is seeking institutional support from IN-SPACe.
2. Taramandal's orbital satellite data centre prototype is designed with modules assembled by robotic welding.
3. The National Tourism Mart–2025 in Visakhapatnam was organised by the AP Tourism Department with the Federation of Associations in Indian Tourism and Hospitality (FAITH).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the institutional support being sought is from IN-SPACe; AU Engineering College is the academic collaborator.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the prototype uses modular, stackable modules joined by docking technology, not robotic welding.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the Mart was organised by AP Tourism with ADTOI, not FAITH.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about quantum initiatives in AP:
1. The International Year of Quantum Science and Technology, 2025, marked 100 years of quantum mechanics.
2. At the AI Impact Summit, the proposed AI–Quantum Centre of Excellence with the UN International Computing Centre was to be established by year-end at Amaravati Quantum Valley.
3. The APSCHE quantum training initiative aims to train about 100+ faculty and 10,000 students.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the year marked 100 years of quantum mechanics; the APSCHE quantum initiative was aligned with it.
Statement 2: Correct: the Centre was proposed for Amaravati Quantum Valley as an AI–Quantum Digital Embassy.
Statement 3: Incorrect: APSCHE plans to train 1,000+ faculty and about 1,00,000 students, not 100+ and 10,000.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about Amaravati Quantum Valley and tourism:
1. The internship collaboration of the Amaravati Quantum Valley was between TCS and T-Hub.
2. The ground-breaking ceremony for Quantum Valley near Uddandarayunipalem in Amaravati was held on 7 February 2026.
3. The National Tourism Mart–2025 was scheduled to be hosted in Narsapuram on 13–14 February 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the internship collaboration was IBM with T-Hub, not TCS; IBM and TCS formed the jury.
Statement 2: Correct: the foundation-laying of Quantum Valley took place on 7 February 2026 near Uddandarayunipalem.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Visakhapatnam, not Narsapuram, was the host city; Narsapuram is associated with crochet lace.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about AP tourism and TTD probes:
1. The TTD-related controversies in 2025 were probed by the CBI-led SIT, CID, ACB and FSSAI.
2. The tourism segments highlighted at the National Tourism Mart–2025 were coastal, spiritual, heritage, eco-adventure and tribal tourism.
3. The principal aim of the National Tourism Mart–2025 in Visakhapatnam was to boost domestic tourism through B2B networking, destination presentations and FAM trips.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the probes involved the CBI-led SIT, CID, ACB and FSSAI.
Statement 2: Correct: the Mart highlighted coastal, spiritual, heritage, eco-adventure and tribal tourism (e.g. Araku, Lambasingi, Maredumalli).
Statement 3: Correct: the Mart aimed to boost domestic tourism through B2B networking, destination presentations and familiarisation (FAM) trips.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh in news:

Statement 1: Correct: the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways informed Parliament about the four major ports under construction in AP.
Statement 2: Correct: the 57th Formation Day of Prakasam district was observed at Ongole as a tribute to Tanguturi Prakasam Pantulu.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the MoU was signed by Minister T. G. Bharat and FLO President Poonam Sharma, not the CII AP Chairperson.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about Prakasam district's Formation Day:

2. Four-laning of the road to Bestavaripeta was identified as a priority.

**CBG** (Compressed Bio-Gas) plants were listed for green energy.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about the Krishna basin:

n: Krishna basin: Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, AP; disputes under ISRWD Act, 1956 [February 2026 · CM objects to raising Almatti Dam height]

101.s: With reference to Andhra Pradesh’s coastal forest protection measures, identify the incorrect statement.
o: Nearly 10,000 acres of unclassified mangrove forests were identified through satellite imagery.
The identified mangrove forests are to be notified as protected forests.
The road map for the task force was scheduled for completion by the end of February.
A special inter-departmental task force was proposed for the initiative.

101.tq: Negative / Incorrect Statement · tests the “Mangrove protection” angle
n: Mangroves: nearly 10,000 acres of unclassified mangrove forests identified via satellite imagery — to be notified as protected forests [January 2026 · Coastal forest protection and mangroves]
Task force: special inter-departmental task force; road map by end of January [January 2026 · Coastal forest protection and mangroves]
xs: The incorrect statement: road map due by **end of February** — option **(3)**; the notes say **end of January**.
Nearly **10,000 acres** of **unclassified mangroves** were found via **satellite imagery**.
They are to be notified as **protected forests**, under a special **inter-departmental task force**.
xa: The directive came from Deputy CM **K. Pawan Kalyan**.
Flagship programmes: **Great Green Wall of Andhra Pradesh** and **50% Green Cover Programme**.
**MISHTI** was launched in **2023** by **MoEFCC**.

101.s:

3. Andhra Pradesh's first Generation Z-themed post office was set up at Andhra University, Visakhapatnam.

101.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, not Sankhabrata Bagchi, made the announcement.
Statement 2: Correct: the rule requires helmets for both the rider and the pillion passenger on a two-wheeler.
Statement 3: Correct: AP's first Gen Z-themed post office was set up at Andhra University, Visakhapatnam.

101.s: Which of the following statements regarding the memorials announced for Potti Sriramulu is incorrect?
o: His residence will be memorialised at Vijayawada.
The Statue of Sacrifice will be 58 feet high and located at Amaravati.
The building where Potti Sriramulu fasted will be memorialised at Chennai.
Smruthi Vanam will be established at Amaravati.
101.x: The incorrect statement is that his residence will be memorialised at Vijayawada; the correct location is Nellore. Smruthi Vanam and the 58-foot Statue of Sacrifice are planned at Amaravati, while the building where he fasted is at Chennai.
101.tq: Negative / Incorrect Statement · tests the “Memorials and locations” angle
n: Memorial: Smruthi Vanam; Place: Amaravati [December 2025 · December 15 declared "Day of Sacrifice" for Potti Sriramulu]
Memorial: "Statue of Sacrifice" — 58 feet high (days of fasting); Place: Amaravati [December 2025 · December 15 declared "Day of Sacrifice" for Potti Sriramulu]
Memorial: Building where he fasted; Place: Chennai [December 2025 · December 15 declared "Day of Sacrifice" for Potti Sriramulu]
Memorial: His residence; Place: Nellore [December 2025 · December 15 declared "Day of Sacrifice" for Potti Sriramulu]
xs: The incorrect statement: **residence memorialised at Vijayawada** — option **(1)**; his residence is at **Nellore**.
**Smruthi Vanam** and the **58 feet** **"Statue of Sacrifice"** are at **Amaravati**.
The building where he fasted is in **Chennai**.
xa: The statue's **58 feet** height matches his **58-day** fast.
**December 15** is the **"Day of Sacrifice"**.
⚠ Dec 15 is linked to **Andhra State (1953)**, not AP (1956).

101.s:
Consider the following statements about Potti Sriramulu and Andhra:
1. The annual observance of December 15 as the "Day of Sacrifice" was announced at a memorial programme in Kurnool.
2. Andhra State was formed with Hyderabad as its capital.
3. India's aircraft fleet is projected to double to about 1,700 by 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the announcement was made at Sriramulu's Atmarpana Day programme in Vijayawada, not Kurnool.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Andhra State (1953) had Kurnool as its capital, not Hyderabad.
Statement 3: Correct: the fleet is projected to double to about 1,700 by 2030, not 2026.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about AP's coast and environment:
1. The South Coast Railway zone, to start from 1 April, will have its headquarters at Visakhapatnam.
2. Aenictus chittoorensis and Aenictus lankamallensis were the two new army ant species discovered around Sri Venkateswara Wildlife Sanctuary.
3. The Great Green Wall of Andhra Pradesh envisages a bioshield about 5 km wide along a coastline of 974 km.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x:
Statement 1: Correct: South Coast Railway will be headquartered at Visakhapatnam; East Coast Railway (2003) is headquartered at Bhubaneswar.
Statement 2: Correct: the newly discovered species are Aenictus chittoorensis and Aenictus lankamallensis.
Statement 3: Correct: launched by the AP Forest Department, it envisages a 5 km-wide bioshield along the 974 km coastline.

101.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF) was renamed Digital Bharat Nidhi in 2023.
2. BharatNet began in 2011 as NOFN and was renamed in 2015.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
101.x: Both are correct: USOF became Digital Bharat Nidhi in 2023, and NOFN (2011) was renamed BharatNet in 2015.
n: DBN renamed in 2023 from USOF; BharatNet began 2011 as NOFN, renamed 2015 [February 2026 · Amended BharatNet Programme — MoU with AP]
xa: **DoT** via **Digital Bharat Nidhi** signed the amended BharatNet MoU with AP at **Tadepalli**.
Centre sanctioned **₹2,432 crore**; SPV is **AP BharatNet Infrastructure Ltd (APBIL)**.
Signatories: DBN Administrator **Shyamal Mishra** and Spl CS **M.T. Krishna Babu**.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about coastal green cover initiatives:
1. Dr. Nori Dattatreya directed that the green-cover initiative be fast-tracked and unclassified mangroves be protected in Andhra Pradesh.
2. The Great Green Wall of Andhra Pradesh has three zones: mangroves at river mouths, windbreaks on canal bunds and roads, and urban forestry.
3. MISHTI was launched in 2023 by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change after India joined the Mangrove Alliance for Climate at COP27, and covers coastline and salt pan lands.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the directive was issued by Deputy CM and Forest & Environment Minister K. Pawan Kalyan, not Dr. Nori Dattatreya.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the third zone is village agroforestry, not urban forestry.
Statement 3: Correct: MISHTI was launched in 2023 by the MoEF&CC after India joined the Mangrove Alliance for Climate at COP27.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about AP water aerodromes and TTD:
1. The AP Maritime Board was allowed to prepare the Terms of Reference for seven proposed water aerodromes in Andhra Pradesh.
2. Three locations were proposed for Phase 2 of Andhra Pradesh's water aerodromes.
3. The primary objective of the Sacred Herbal Garden proposed by TTD in Tirumala is to display 12 iconic wild animal species of Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the MoEF&CC Expert Appraisal Committee allowed AP Airports Development Corporation Ltd, not the AP Maritime Board, to prepare the ToR.
Statement 2: Correct: Phase 2 proposed three locations; seven locations were identified in Phase 1.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the garden is intended to conserve rare and endangered medicinal plants of the Seshachalam forests.

101.s:
Assertion (A): Andaman and Nicobar is to get the country's first-ever water aerodromes.
Reason (R): The EIA Notification, 2006 makes EIA mandatory for water aerodromes.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
101.x: The Assertion is correct: Andaman and Nicobar is to get the country's first-ever water aerodromes. The Reason is false because the EIA Notification, 2006 is stated to make EIA mandatory for mining, thermal power and river valley projects, not specifically for water aerodromes.
101.tq: Assertion-Reason · tests the “First water aerodromes and EIA” angle
n: ⚠ Andaman and Nicobar to get the country's first-ever water aerodromes [December 2025 · ToR for seven water aerodromes in AP]
EIA Notification, 2006: EIA mandatory for mining, thermal power, river valley projects [December 2025 · ToR for seven water aerodromes in AP]
xs: **A is true, but R is false** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **Andaman and Nicobar** is to get the country's **first-ever** water aerodromes.
R is false: the **EIA Notification, 2006** mandates EIA for **mining, thermal power, river valley projects** — not water aerodromes.
xa: AP's **seven** water aerodromes got ToR approval as a first step to EIA clearance.
Conditions: **early public hearings** and an **Indian Navy** NOC for Visakhapatnam.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about TTD and South Coast Railway:
1. Sandeep Mathur is the General Manager of South Coast Railway.
2. In the Anga Vastram scam at TTD, polyester shawls were passed off as pure mulberry silk.
3. The proposed TTD Sacred Herbal Garden in Tirumala will be designed with 13 thematic zones.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Sandeep Mathur is the General Manager of South Coast Railway.
Statement 2: Correct: the polyester shawls were passed off as pure mulberry silk, not pure cotton.
Statement 3: Correct: the garden will have 13 thematic zones covering health, spiritual traditions and ecology.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about infrastructure and development projects:
1. The One District One Product initiative was launched in 1999.
2. After the South Coast Railway zone reorganisation, South Central Railway retained the Secunderabad, Hyderabad and Raichur divisions.
3. Railway connectivity is not one of the five pillars of Sagarmala.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
101.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the ODOP initiative was launched in 2018, not 1999.
Statement 2: Incorrect: South Central Railway retained the Nanded division, not Raichur, along with Secunderabad and Hyderabad.
Statement 3: Correct: the five pillars are port modernisation, port connectivity, port-led industrialisation, coastal community development, and coastal shipping and IWT; railway connectivity is not one.

101.s: With reference to the Gangavaram Port iron-ore blending MoU and APSRTC, which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Dedicated iron ore blending plant – Gangavaram Port
101.x: NMDC was established in 1958; 1942 is Vale S.A.'s year of establishment.
n: Adani Gangavaram Port (APSEZ) signed MoU with NMDC and Brazil's Vale S.A. at India–Brazil Business Forum, Delhi — dedicated iron ore blending plant at Gangavaram Port [February 2026 · Gangavaram iron ore blending MoU and handloom projects]
NMDC: est. 1958, HQ Hyderabad; Vale: est. 1942, Rio de Janeiro [February 2026 · Gangavaram iron ore blending MoU and handloom projects]
APSRTC: est. 1958, HQ Vijayawada [February 2026 · AP appointments — Chief Secretary and others]
xa: The MoU was signed at the **India–Brazil Business Forum**, Delhi, by **Adani Gangavaram Port (APSEZ)**.
**NMDC** HQ is **Hyderabad**; **Vale** is based in **Rio de Janeiro**.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh developments in 2025–26:
1. Pallepandaga 2.0, announced by Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan, comprises 53,382 works with an outlay of ₹6,700 crore.
2. Dagadarthi greenfield airport, approved by the AP Cabinet in January 2026, is in Nellore district.
3. The legacy issues associated with TTD in 2025 were digital payments, adulterated ghee in laddu prasadam and engineering works.

101.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Pallepandaga 2.0 comprises 53,382 works with an outlay of ₹6,700 crore.
Statement 2: Correct: Dagadarthi airport is in Nellore district, near Krishnapatnam and Ramayapatnam ports.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the legacy issues were Parakamani cash-counting irregularities, adulterated ghee and engineering works; digital payments was a reform, not a legacy issue.

101.s: Which of the following ports under construction in Andhra Pradesh is INCORRECTLY matched with its district?
101.x: Ramayapatnam is in SPSR Nellore district, not Prakasam.
n: Port: Mulapeta (formerly Bhavanapadu); District: Srikakulam [February 2026 · Four major ports under construction in AP]
Port: Machilipatnam; District: Krishna [February 2026 · Four major ports under construction in AP]
Port: Ramayapatnam; District: SPSR Nellore [February 2026 · Four major ports under construction in AP]
Port: Kakinada SEZ Port; District: Kakinada [February 2026 · Four major ports under construction in AP]
xa: ⚠ **Mulapeta** was formerly called **Bhavanapadu**.
The **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways** informed Parliament about these ports.
**Sagarmala** has **5 pillars**, including port-led industrialisation and coastal shipping and IWT.

101.s: Which of the following statements regarding the projects highlighted for Prakasam district is incorrect?
o: The Veligonda project draws Srisailam floodwater for drinking and irrigation in Prakasam, Nellore and Kadapa.
The Paleru project has been fast-tracked in Prakasam district.
The Korisapadu lift-irrigation project is located in Palnadu district.
Donakonda is being developed as an industrial hub with a large land bank.

n: Project: Veligonda (Poola Subbaiah); Detail: draws Srisailam floodwater — drinking/irrigation for Prakasam, Nellore, Kadapa [February 2026 · Prakasam district 57th Formation Day — budget priorities]
Project: Paleru; Detail: Prakasam district — fast-tracked [February 2026 · Prakasam district 57th Formation Day — budget priorities]

**Donakonda** is an industrial hub with a large land bank.

Prakasam is a hub for **FCV (Flue-Cured Virginia)** tobacco.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh water projects:
1. Almatti Dam, whose height increase Karnataka proposed, is the main reservoir of the Upper Krishna Irrigation Project.
2. The Polavaram project required inter-state coordination with Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
3. Konaseema is a Phase 1 location for water aerodromes in Andhra Pradesh.

101.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Almatti is the main reservoir of the Upper Krishna Irrigation Project; CM Naidu objected to raising its height.
Statement 2: Incorrect: inter-state coordination was required with Telangana and Chhattisgarh, not Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Konaseema is a Phase 2 location; Phase 1 includes Prakasam Barrage, Srisailam Dam, Lambasingi, Rushikonda, Kakinada, Jalaput and Gandikota.

101.s:
Assertion (A): The headworks of the Polavaram project are 80% completed.
Reason (R): Polavaram is a National Multipurpose Irrigation Project on the Godavari.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
101.x: Both the assertion and the reason are true: the headworks are 80% completed, and Polavaram is a National Multipurpose Irrigation Project on the Godavari. However, the project’s classification does not explain the stated percentage of headworks completion.
101.tq: Assertion-Reason · tests the “Project status and classification” angle
n: Headworks: 80% completed [December 2025 · Polavaram project — completion by July 2027]
Status: National Multipurpose Irrigation Project on the Godavari [December 2025 · Polavaram project — completion by July 2027]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.

R: it is a **National Multipurpose Irrigation Project** on the **Godavari** — its status does not explain the progress figure.

CM **Naidu** set a **July 2027** target, ahead of the **December 2027** deadline.

The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) recently introduced a national standard to test and assess bomb disposal systems.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. The new standard is known as IS 19445:2025.
2. It will improve interoperability of equipment across agencies.
3. It was developed by TBRL, DRDO in collaboration with the 30th Central Scientific Research Institute, Russia. Select the answer using the code given below:
42.x: Statement 1 is correct: The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) recently notified India's first dedicated national standard for bomb disposal systems, officially designated as IS 19445:2025. It establishes comprehensive guidelines for evaluating bomb disposal systems (like bomb blankets, baskets, and inhibitors) against blast loads and splinter effects. Statement 2 is correct: A primary objective of this standard is to bring uniformity in evaluation practices. By establishing a transparent and uniform basis for procurement, testing, and certification, it aims to significantly improve the reliability and Science and Technology PMF IAS S&T – 99 interoperability of equipment used across various security units (such as the Armed Forces, Central Armed Police Forces, and State Police). Statement 3 is incorrect: The standard was not developed in collaboration with a Russian institute. It was developed indigenously by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) at the request of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the Terminal Ballistics Research Laboratory (TBRL), DRDO. TBRL served as the convenor for the expert panel (under the Arms and Ammunition for Civilian Use Sectional Committee), working with Indian stakeholders such as the Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPR&D) to adapt global best practices to Indian threat scenarios and operational conditions.

xa: Cumulative **125 bps** cut since **February 2025**.

35.s: Which of the following rice-production interventions is correctly matched?

35.s:
Arrange the following developments in India's cryptocurrency policy in chronological order:
A. RBI banking ban
B. Supreme Court lifted the RBI ban
C. 30% tax on gains, 1% TDS and e₹ pilots
D. Exchanges brought under FIU-IND for KYC/AML
35.x: The correct sequence is A-B-C-D: the RBI banking ban was in 2018, the Supreme Court lifted it in 2020, the tax and e₹ pilot measures followed in 2022, and exchanges came under FIU-IND in 2023. The nearest distractor reverses the 2018 and 2020 developments.
35.tq: Chronological Ordering · tests the “India's crypto-policy timeline” angle
n: Year: 2018; India: RBI banking ban [December 2025 · Bitcoin's slide after October record and crypto regulation]
Year: 2020; India: Supreme Court lifted RBI ban [December 2025 · Bitcoin's slide after October record and crypto regulation]
Year: 2022; India: 30% tax on gains + 1% TDS; Virtual Digital Assets, not legal tender; e₹ (CBDC) pilots [December 2025 · Bitcoin's slide after October record and crypto regulation]
Year: 2023; India: Exchanges under FIU-IND (KYC/AML) [December 2025 · Bitcoin's slide after October record and crypto regulation]
xs: Order **A-B-C-D** — option **(4)**.
**2018** RBI banking ban → **2020** **Supreme Court** lifted it → **2022** **30%** tax, **1% TDS**, **e₹** pilots → **2023** exchanges under **FIU-IND**.
xa: Crypto in India = **Virtual Digital Assets**, not legal tender.
**Digital Rupee:** **1 e₹ = 1 ₹**; issued by **RBI**.
Legal tender abroad: **El Salvador**, **Central African Republic**.

35.s: With reference to the revised MSME definition introduced from 1 April 2025, identify the incorrect statement.

Enterprise: Small; Investment old → new: 10 → 25; Turnover old → new: 50 → 100 [January 2026 · Year End Review 2025 — Ministry of MSME]

With reference to Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), consider the following statements:
1. All types of UAVs can do vertical landing.
2. All types of UAVs can do automated hovering.
3. All types of UAVs can use battery only as a source of power supply.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: Statement 1 is incorrect: Only certain types of UAVs (like multirotors or VTOL drones) can do vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL). Fixed-wing UAVs generally require a runway or catapult to take off and land, not vertical landing. Statement 2 is incorrect: Multirotor UAVs can hover. But fixed-wing UAVs cannot hover – they need forward motion to generate lift. So not all UAVs can hover autonomously. Statement 3 is incorrect: Some UAVs use internal combustion engines, hybrid systems, or solar power. A battery is common, but not the only power source for all UAVs. PMF Concept Hack: All three statements use the word "All", which is a major red flag in technology questions. Unmanned Aerial Vehicle types are very diverse—some can do vertical landing and hovering (like quadcopters), while many cannot. Science and Technology PMF IAS S&T – 104 Similarly, UAVs can run on fuel, hybrid systems, or solar power, not just batteries. Since all three statements are overgeneralized, none are correct → (d)

Consider the following statements:
1. Statement I: Some rare earth elements are used in the manufacture of flat television screens and computer monitors.
2. Statement II: Some rare earth elements have phosphorescent properties. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct, but Statement II is correct
55.x: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, and Statement II explains Statement I: Rare earth elements such as europium, terbium, and yttrium are used in flat-screen televisions and computer monitors. Some rare earth elements also exhibit phosphorescence, which helps produce bright colours and display effects. Human and Economic Geography PMF IAS Geo – 45 PMF Concept Hack: The key trigger here is the word "some" in both statements. It makes both statements nonabsolute and partially true by nature, which makes direct negation difficult in UPSC logic—because you cannot confidently say "no rare earth element has these properties or uses." Statement I is correct because rare-earth elements are used in flat screens and computer monitors for their optical and electronic properties. Statement II is also correct because certain rare earth elements exhibit phosphorescent properties, which is the scientific basis for their use in display technologies. Now the link between them is important: Statement II directly explains Statement I because phosphorescence is the key property that makes rare earth elements useful in display screens.

The term critical minerals includes minerals that are strategically important for modern technologies, and Rare Earth Elements are among the most discussed critical minerals globally. So saying REEs are not included in critical minerals is unlikely. Once Statement 4 is eliminated, only options (a) and (b) remain. At this stage, you do not even need to worry much about Statement 3. 82.x: Kerala, not Karnataka, introduced the first Comprehensive Urban Policy; Kerala's Graphene Policy with the Kalamassery centre is correctly stated.

xa: Kerala's urban policy expects urban population of **~80% by 2050**.
**'Graphene Aurora'** is by **Digital University Kerala** (**₹94.85 crore**).
⚠ Both the urban policy and graphene policy firsts belong to **Kerala**.

n: Yuga: Satya; Somnath temple built by: Gold — Chandra (Soma) [January 2026 · Bhadrakali Temple inscription — Somnath legacy]

82.s: Which of the following statements about International Data Privacy Day and India's data-protection framework is incorrect?
o: The DPDP Act was enacted on 13 November 2025.
Convention 108 is regarded as the world's first legally binding international data protection treaty.
The IT Act, 2000 includes Section 69A for blocking.
82.x: The incorrect statement is that the DPDP Act was enacted on 13 November 2025; it was enacted on 11 August 2023. 13 November 2025 was the date on which the DPDP Rules were notified, making it the tempting confusion.
82.tq: Negative / Incorrect Statement · tests the “Theme” angle
n: Commemorates Convention 108 — world's first legally binding international data protection treaty [January 2026 · International Data Privacy Day — 28 January]
IT Act 2000: Sec 69A (blocking), 70B (CERT-In) [January 2026 · International Data Privacy Day — 28 January]

DPDP Act 2023: enacted 11 August 2023; SARAL approach; Data Protection Board of India; response within 90 days; verifiable parental consent for children [January 2026 · International Data Privacy Day — 28 January]
DPDP Rules 2025: notified 13 November 2025 [January 2026 · International Data Privacy Day — 28 January]
Theme 2026: "Privacy by Design" [January 2026 · International Data Privacy Day — 28 January]

1. Ibrahimpatnam and Penuganchiprolu blocks of NTR district won NITI Aayog gold medals under the Aspirational Blocks Programme for 100% results in six indicators.
2. According to the Air Quality Life Index 2025 findings, Visakhapatnam recorded PM2.5 concentrations of 40–50 µg/m³.
3. The Integrated Command and Control Centre at Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams was inaugurated by N. Chandrababu Naidu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x:
Statement 1: Correct: Ibrahimpatnam and Penuganchiprolu blocks of NTR district received the gold medals.
Statement 2: Correct: Visakhapatnam recorded 40–50 µg/m³, not 30–40 µg/m³.
Statement 3: Correct: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu inaugurated the centre, which uses over 6,000 CCTV cameras.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about Swachha Andhra and smart kitchens:
1. The Swachha Andhra Awards–2025 cover only industries, NGOs and urban development authorities.
2. Under the Swarna Andhra–Swachha Andhra campaign, Swachha Andhra Day is observed every third Saturday.
3. India's first Centralised Advanced Smart Kitchen at CK Dinne in Kadapa district was established at a cost of ₹2 crore, with solar power and an RO plant.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the awards cover municipalities, gram panchayats, schools, hospitals and several other institutions, while NGOs and sanitation workers are recognised as "Swachhata Warriors".
Statement 2: Correct: every third Saturday is observed as Swachha Andhra Day.
Statement 3: Correct: the smart kitchen cost ₹2 crore and is solar powered with an RO plant.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh in the news:
1. According to the AQLI 2025 context, Andhra Pradesh's average PM2.5 concentration remained at 17.8 µg/m³ from 1998 to 2021.
2. The P4 initiative highlighted by Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu refers to the People–Private–Public Partnership for the Poor.
3. Tirupati became the first city in Andhra Pradesh to launch the City Visitor Information and Record Management System (CVIRMS).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: Andhra Pradesh's average PM2.5 concentration rose from 17.8 µg/m³ in 1998 to more than 30 µg/m³ in 2021, a rise of over 70%.
Statement 2: Correct: P4 stands for People–Private–Public Partnership for the Poor.
Statement 3: Correct: Tirupati was first in AP to launch CVIRMS, requiring hotels, lodges and homestays to record visitor IDs digitally.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about AP surveillance and security:
1. CVIRMS gives instant alerts about persons with a criminal background because it is linked to a police database.
2. NTR district became the first in Andhra Pradesh to achieve 100% CCTV coverage of all its inhabited villages.
3. Under NTR district's 100% CCTV coverage drive, at least six cameras were installed in each inhabited village.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x:
Statement 1: Correct: CVIRMS is linked to a police database to provide instant criminal-background alerts.
Statement 2: Correct: NTR district achieved it, with at least four cameras in each of its 305 inhabited villages.
Statement 3: Incorrect: at least four cameras, not six, were installed in each of the district's 305 inhabited villages.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about AP temples, rice cards and canteens:
1. Annadanam, already available in 7 temples, is being extended to all 23 major temples in Andhra Pradesh.
2. In Andhra Pradesh, the eKYC exemption for rice cards applies to seniors above 80.
3. The Trupti Canteens initiative of Andhra Pradesh is implemented under MEPMA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x:
Statement 1: Correct: adding 16 more temples to the existing 7 brings Annadanam to all 23 major temples.
Statement 2: Correct: the eKYC exemption applies to seniors above 80, not above 70.
Statement 3: Correct: Trupti Canteens are implemented under MEPMA (Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas).

89.s:
The AP-UNICEF youth programmes are aligned with:
1. 'One Entrepreneur, One Family' and Swarna Andhra 2030.
2. 'One Entrepreneur, One Village' and Swarna Andhra 2047.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
89.x: Neither: the alignment is with 'One Entrepreneur, One Family' and Swarna Andhra 2047.
n: Aligned with: 'One Entrepreneur, One Family' and Swarna Andhra 2047 [May 2025 · AP-UNICEF youth programmes — YFSI, YouthHub, Passport to Earning]
xa: **YFSI** — **2 lakh**+ students, **UPSHIFT** framework.
**Passport to Earning** — youth aged **15–29**.
**YouthHub** linked with **Naipunyam** portal.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about AP Annadanam, canteens and youth programmes:
1. The Tirumala Vengamamba Annadanam model is being used as the benchmark for the expanded Annadanam programme in Andhra Pradesh.
2. Under the AP–UNICEF youth programmes, YouthHub is the digital, multilingual platform integrated with Andhra Pradesh's Naipunyam portal.
3. The Trupti Canteens initiative in Andhra Pradesh is linked to YouthHub.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Tirumala Vengamamba Annadanam model is the benchmark for the expanded programme.
Statement 2: Correct: YouthHub is the digital, multilingual platform integrated with Andhra Pradesh's Naipunyam portal.
Statement 3: Incorrect: Trupti Canteens are linked to the Smart Street Programme; YouthHub belongs to the AP–UNICEF youth programmes.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about AP rice cards and MEPMA:
1. eKYC exemption is not one of the six rice-card services offered through Village and Ward Secretariats in AP.
2. Antyodaya Anna Yojana cards providing 35 kg of rice were identified for transgender persons, separated spouses and orphans.
3. The SHG Profiling App is not among MEPMA's four new urban livelihood initiatives.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the six services are new card, bifurcation, change of address, addition and removal of members and surrender; eKYC exemption is a separate provision.
Statement 2: Incorrect: AAY cards providing 35 kg of rice were identified for Chenchus, Yanadis and pensioned rural artists.
Statement 3: Correct: the four initiatives are Rapido, Trupti Hotels, Smart Street and Green Livelihoods; the SHG Profiling App belongs to MEPMA's profiling system.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about TUDA and the 104 service:
1. TUDA, whose land acquisition, layout planning, zoning and parks were reviewed by the CAG, is a statutory body under the AP Urban Development Authorities Act.
2. During its visit to TUDA on 28 May 2025, the CAG delegation recommended complete digitisation of TUDA's layout approvals.
3. Under the restructured 104 Mobile Medical Unit service in Andhra Pradesh, 35 confirmatory tests are offered at the doorstep.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x:
Statement 1: Correct: TUDA is a statutory body under the Andhra Pradesh Urban Development Authorities Act.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the CAG recommended completing digitisation of TUDA's financial and accounting systems; layouts were only reviewed.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the restructured 104 service provides 47 confirmatory tests at the doorstep; 35 is the number of persons screened by each vehicle per day.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's recent initiatives:
1. The Andhra Pradesh delegation for the National Efficient Cooking Programme was led by A. Surya Kumari.
2. As on 31 December 2025, the number of districts in Andhra Pradesh increased from 26 to 28.
3. The primary objective of the P4 programme of Andhra Pradesh is the expansion of cardiac-care facilities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the AP delegation was led by A. Surya Kumari; WCD Secretary Anil Malik and BEE praised the initiative.
Statement 2: Correct: two new districts took the total from 26 to 28, and the boundaries of 17 districts changed.
Statement 3: Incorrect: P4, or Public-Private-People Partnership, aims at the complete eradication of poverty.

89.s: Sri Padmavati Mahila Visvavidyalayam, Tirupati, received ISO certifications. Which pair (standard – area) is correctly matched?

Standard: ISO 21001:2018; Area: Educational Organisation Management [April 2025 · Sri Padmavati Mahila Visvavidyalayam gets three ISO certifications]

89.s: With reference to the P4 programme, which pair (level – leadership) is correctly matched?
89.x: Pawan Kalyan is Vice-Chairperson of the State society; N. Chandrababu Naidu chairs it, District In-charge Ministers coordinate districts and MLAs constituencies.
n: State society: Chairperson CM N. Chandrababu Naidu; Vice-Chairperson Deputy CM Pawan Kalyan; CEO, Director, call centre [April 2025 · P4 programme — State-level society headed by CM]
District: District In-charge Ministers; constituency: MLAs; village/ward: Panchayat / Ward Administrative Secretaries [April 2025 · P4 programme — State-level society headed by CM]
